subject: Coord: Witnessing window and evidence schedule for Private Deployment
messages:
From: Alan Bryce <alan.bryce@healthcorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthCorp Legal <healthcorp-legal@example.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — evidence / witnessing window request

Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Our legal team has one more ask before we can sign the order form: they want a brief, mutually agreed "witnessing window" for the operator-runbook acceptance and a list of evidence artifacts Redwood will provide at handover (for our auditors). Can you confirm:

- A 2-week window when HealthCorp auditors can perform a remote witnessing session?
- A compact evidence bundle list (for e-discovery and SOC-style review): snapshots, access logs, operator checklist, and a signed runbook?
- Whether Redwood is open to an escrow-lite arrangement (trusted third-party escrow of a sealed snapshot) for the narrow case of insolvency / breach?

We aim to get this into our MSA exhibit and the Order Form schedule. Appreciate a short timeline and any constraints.

Best,
Alan
Director, IT Procurement
HealthCorp

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alan Bryce <alan.bryce@healthcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence / witnessing window request

Alan — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned in principle and can support a formal witnessing window and an evidence bundle. High level proposal:

- Witnessing window: 10 business days (HealthCorp picks any contiguous 10 business-day period within 45 days of order activation). Remote sessions via shared screen + dry-run playback of the snapshot restore.
- Evidence bundle (delivered over secure link):
  * Sealed base snapshot (read-only) + hash verifier
  * Operator runbook (signed PDF) — see attached draft
  * System access logs for the witness window timeframe (redacted per PII rules)
  * Order-form-specific test playbook and acceptance checklist
- Escrow-lite: Redwood is open to a sealed snapshot deposit with a neutral custodian (we've worked with EscrowTrust previously). Custody triggers limited to insolvency, prolonged breach, or mutually agreed forensic need. We will need specific carveouts for operator credentials and real-time secrets.

I've attached a draft runbook and an evidence checklist for your review. I'll loop in Hannah from Legal Ops and Marissa from Product Ops to work through timing and any MSA exhibit language. Can you confirm HealthCorp's preferred 10-day windows in the next 5 business days?

Regards,
Irene
Head, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alan Bryce <alan.bryce@healthcorp.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, HealthCorp Legal <healthcorp-legal@example.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence / witnessing window request

Alan / team — quick note from legal ops on MSA redlines and practical constraints:

1) Escrow-lite: we can support a sealed snapshot deposit with EscrowTrust. Proposed language: custodial deposit + release conditions limited to (a) insolvency, (b) court order, (c) mutually agreed forensic investigation. Redwood reserves the right to redact secrets and private keys; those remain under Redwood custody and would only be made available under explicit multi-party checks.

2) Snapshot frequency and retention: Redwood proposes a single pre-handover sealed snapshot plus a short retention (90 days) in the custodian vault. HealthCorp can request additional scheduled snapshots as a paid add-on.

3) Witnessing logistics: we cannot provide direct console access; remote witnessing will be via recorded restore + operator-led demo. Any temporary console access for auditors requires a separate, time-limited access plan and indemnity language.

Attached: annotated MSA exhibit with our suggested carve language and a redline doc (msa_redlines_20280814.docx). Please review and let us know which items you need escalated to procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Hannah
Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Alan Bryce <alan.bryce@healthcorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthCorp Legal <healthcorp-legal@example.com>, Cassandra Wells <cassandra.wells@escrowtrust.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence / witnessing window request

Thanks Hannah — that helps. A few follow-ups from HealthCorp Legal:

- We need the escrow release conditions expanded to include "verified material breach of data handling obligations" (we can provide proposed language).
- 90-day custodian retention is short for our auditors; would Redwood consider 180 days for the initial project?
- For operator credential redaction: HealthCorp requests an attested statement from Redwood certifying the redaction process and test steps that prove the snapshot remains reconstructable for auditors (without exposing secrets).

Cassandra — can EscrowTrust confirm standard retention options (90/180/365 days) and whether you can hold a sealed snapshot with pre-committed release checks?

We can confirm potential witnessing windows after we sort the retention and release language.

Regards,
Alan

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alan Bryce <alan.bryce@healthcorp.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, HealthCorp Legal <healthcorp-legal@example.com>, Cassandra Wells <cassandra.wells@escrowtrust.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Aug 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence / witnessing window request

Team — next steps and commitments from Redwood:

1) Retention: Redwood can extend custodian retention to 180 days for this deal (HC-2028-145) without a charge for the first year. We'll document this in an Order Form exhibit.

2) Escrow release trigger: we can accept the additional release trigger for "verified material breach of data handling obligations" with a mutually agreed verification procedure to avoid unilateral releases. We'll ask legal to draft the verification steps.

3) Attestation: Redwood will provide a signed attestation describing the redaction process and the reconstruction test procedure. We'll attach a test report from our internal verification run during the witness session.

4) Witnessing logistics: HealthCorp to propose two candidate 10-business-day windows; Redwood will confirm within 2 business days of proposal. Remote session format and agenda will be provided in advance.

Attached: operator_runbook_v1.pdf and evidence_checklist.xlsx (working drafts). Marissa / David — please prepare the acceptance agenda and a short timeline for ops prep. Hannah — please coordinate final MSA exhibit redlines and circulate a version for signature when ready.

I'll set a short sync for next week if helpful.

Thanks,
Irene
Head, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
